messages.content:
Return only the deliverable. Use short, plain, complete sentences. Lead with the answer. A memo is a short standalone paragraph, not a form: add no heading, subject line, label, preface or conclusion. Say each fact once. Aim for 60–80 words from a long source, but keep all facts even if that needs more words.

Meaning comes before length. Preserve every unique source fact: results, limits, exclusions, unknowns, evidence, owners, next actions and prerequisites. Copy technical strings character for character, including spaces and hyphens. Preserve negations, numbers, units, commands, errors, filenames, fields, frontmatter and code blocks. Never invent or infer a completed action.

Copy an already concise source EXACTLY, with no added words. Return requested JSON alone with exact keys and types. Explicit requests for detail override brevity: include ordered steps, reasons, conditions and provenance. Check the final text against every source sentence for missing information.

Existing memo rewrites require an explicit request, preview and approved save through validated memo.write with expected_revision. Stop on conflict; preserve newer text, source transcripts and detailed evidence. Draft in one normal model call.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: reply.
Reply to a user asking why their saved edit was rejected.

Source:
The save was rejected because the document changed after the version that the user read. The user read revision r17, but revision r18 was current by the time the save reached the publication check. The system preserved the r18 text and did not overwrite it with the stale edit. The rejected edit has not been applied. This was a revision conflict, not a permission denial. The next action is to read r18, compare the intended edit with that version, and submit a new save using r18 as the expected revision if the edit still makes sense. There is no automatic retry. The diagnostic reference is save-check-9. It is not known from that diagnostic who authored r18, and the response should not guess. The user needs an explanation of the conflict and a clear next step, not a long account of implementation internals.

message.content: Your edit was rejected because the document had changed since you last read it. You were working from revision r17, but by the time your save reached the publication check, revision r18 was the current version. The system kept r18 and did not overwrite it with your stale edit, so the change was not applied. This is a revision conflict, not a permission issue. To proceed, open revision r18, compare your intended changes with that version, and submit a new save using r18 as the expected revision if the edit still makes sense. There is no automatic retry. The diagnostic reference for this event is save-check-9.
